channel.title: Humanoids Daily
channel.description: We bring you the latest developments in robotics, with a special focus on humanoid robots and intelligent machines. From groundbreaking research to real-world applications, we cover the people, technologies, and innovations shaping the future of robotics.

item.title: How Frontier Language Models Are Speeding Up Robotics Research
item.description: From a vibe-coded motion tracker to Argon reviewing robot failures and Astra steering GR00T 2, language models now sit in several parts of the robot-learning loop. Most of the fastest gains are still in simulation.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: FORT Robotics, Safety Supplier to Agility, Posts 52% Revenue Growth in S-4 Ahead of Nasdaq Listing
item.description: FORT, which supplies safety systems for Digit, reported $12.5 million in nine-month revenue and an $8.0 million loss as it heads for Nasdaq at a $500 million valuation.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Robotera Opens Orders for XHAND 1 Pro-U, the Hand in NVIDIA's GR00T 2 DexUMI Demos
item.description: Robotera's 16-DoF XHAND 1 Pro-U mirrors NVIDIA's DexUMI exoskeleton joint for joint. It ran the GR00T 2 yogurt, granola and match-lighting demos at CoRL, and the first run is 40 units.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: LG Signs With Korea's Robot Certification Agency to Safety-Test Its Humanoids
item.description: LG Electronics and KIRIA will put CLOiD through a pilot safety certification and build the evaluation system for Korea's first humanoid safety certification centre in Daegu.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Foundation Misses Payroll After CEO Borrowed $4.6 Million to Buy a Home
item.description: Foundation Future Industries has not paid staff since October 30, CNBC reports, after CEO Sankaet Pathak borrowed $4.6 million from the company in 2025. Sources also say its $24 million in Pentagon contracts came with the Boardwalk Robotics acquisition.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: After SuperMimic, Open-Source Humanoid Motion Trackers Now Train in Minutes on One GPU
item.description: A UC Berkeley paper released without code set off a run of community reimplementations. InstantTrack, BlinkMimic and XMimic cut Unitree G1 tracker training on a 40-clip benchmark to a few minutes, in simulation.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: ASUS Unveils Gallop, Its First Humanoid Robot, Already Packing Parts on Its Own Production Line
item.description: The two-armed robot runs on NVIDIA Jetson Thor and learns from head-camera footage of ASUS factory workers. Partner pilots start in 2027, with a market launch targeted for the second half of 2028.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Andy Rubin's Genki Robotics Shows Its Humanoid to Japan's Prime Minister
item.description: Genki Robotics, the Tokyo startup founded by Android creator Andy Rubin, showed its humanoid for the first time at Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's physical AI meeting. The unit walked for the first time three days earlier, and Genki plans an open Android-style platform built on Japanese hardware.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: J.P. Morgan Forecasts 300,000 to 400,000 US-Made Humanoids by 2030
item.description: The bank says supply, not demand, limits the pace, puts humanoid costs near labor parity and favors component suppliers such as Timken, ROBOTIS and Orbbec.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as NVIDIA CEO; CFO Colette Kress Steps In
item.description: Huang left NVIDIA on Thursday after reports of an affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. The board says the product roadmap, including its robotics work, continues without interruption.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Agile Robots Raises $500 Million Series F at $8.5 Billion Valuation
item.description: SoftBank led the round, with NVIDIA and Hitachi joining, as the Munich company plans US expansion and more production capacity in Germany.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: GXO Signs Letter of Intent for Up to 1,000 Apptronik Apollo Humanoids
item.description: GXO and Apptronik will expand Apollo warehouse trials from 2027 under a Robotics-as-a-Service framework, and intend to roll out up to 1,000 robots over four years if agreed KPIs are met.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Six AGIBOT G2 Robots Complete 1,730 Tasks in 24-Hour Shanghai Convenience Store Trial
item.description: Four of the six robots pass a performance assessment as the trial puts customer service, retail operations and embodied AI capabilities to the test in a working store.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Figure's Night-Shift "Robot Babysitter" Is One of About 30 Jobs Keeping Its Humanoids Running
item.description: Figure is hiring a night-shift coordinator to run its humanoids in Santa Clara. Its careers page also lists operators on three shifts, staff for customer sites in Reno and Fontana, teleoperation pilots and a 24/7 data operation in Brazil.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5 Puts Apollo 2 on Mercedes-Benz Lines as Argon Speeds Up Training
item.description: Google DeepMind's new VLA succeeds 30% to 100% more often than Gemini Robotics 2 across 200-plus tasks, and sorted car parts at 96% success on Apptronik's Apollo 2 in two Mercedes-Benz plants. It is going to partners only.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: This Week in Humanoids: Agility on Nasdaq, GR00T 2 and Fable 5.2
item.description: Our November 10 newsletter covers Agility’s Nasdaq debut, NVIDIA’s GR00T 2 at CoRL, Anthropic’s Fable 5.2, Atlas on wheels and Apple’s HALO.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: HD Hyundai Robotics Builds Its Own Robot Brain, as Skild AI Pitches Korea on Building the Bodies
item.description: HD Hyundai Robotics' new dual-arm robot runs a foundation model it trained itself, and Palantir AI agents have cut its problem-resolution time by 63%. In Seoul the same week, Skild AI's Deepak Pathak courted Korean motor makers and described deployments at LG and Market Kurly.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Anthropic Says Claude Fable 5.2 More Than Doubles GPT-6 Astra on a Robot-Control Benchmark
item.description: Anthropic reports 64.9% on the RoboDojo simulated two-arm benchmark, against 29.8% for Astra in its own runs. On RoboDojo's leaderboard, only one agent system scores higher.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Robbyant Open-Sources LingBot-Touch, One Tactile Model for Three Sensor Types
item.description: Ant Group's Robbyant has released LingBot-Touch under Apache 2.0. Across 26 real-robot tasks, its tactile tokens lifted four policies by 14 to 25 points, including on a hand whose sensor it never saw.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: MACHINA Summit Moves to the Palais des Congrès for 2027, Names Wandercraft, Agility and Skild AI Speakers
item.description: The Paris physical AI conference grows to two days and 3,500 expected attendees on 7–8 July 2027, closing with an invitation-only gala at Versailles.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: "Robotics Is No Longer an Elitist Sport": NVIDIA Unveils GR00T 2 and Open-Sources the Stack Behind It
item.description: Jim Fan presented the 2B-parameter model at CoRL. NVIDIA reports 95% success from five demonstrations per task; weights open in December, with data, SimFoundry and hardware designs out now.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Boston Dynamics Puts Atlas on Wheels to Push Its Motors to the Limit
item.description: Boston Dynamics swapped Atlas's feet for scooter wheels on the ankle actuators and retrained its whole-body RL controller to roll, drift and spin-jump. It is a motor stress test, not a product.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: PrimeBOT Builds Its 10,000th Personal Robot, 14 Days After Its 5,000th
item.description: PrimeBOT says its 10,000th Q1 and T1 personal robot rolled off the line on November 8, with daily capacity at 240 units. It has not disclosed sales or deliveries.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Figure’s HQ Is Crawling With Figure 03 Robots. What Are They All Doing?
item.description: Two new videos from Brett Adcock show dozens of Figure 03 humanoids roaming Figure’s headquarters, inside and out. The company is close to having more robots than employees, but has said little about how many are doing paid work.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Atlas Battery Pack to Use 70 Samsung SDI Cells, Report Says
item.description: The reported 1.3 kWh pack adds detail to Atlas’s power system as humanoid makers pursue battery swapping, fast charging and new chemistries.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Inside Unitree's Hangzhou Factory, Robots Are Still Mostly Built by Hand
item.description: Josef Chen's visit to Unitree's Hangzhou factory, and the company's own filings, show a robot maker running on manual assembly with about $50 of machinery per robot. He argues US wages and trade barriers make factory automation far more valuable to American robot makers.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Swiss Startup Embodied AI Unveils AIR, a Wheeled Robot Built to Work Beside Factory Staff Without a Cage
item.description: The EPFL spin-off's two-armed robot starts each job under remote control and, the company says, takes the task over within a month. It reports a 95% average success rate in paid pilots.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Tokyo Researchers Build Robotic Legs With 3D-Printed Muscles, Tendons and Ligaments
item.description: University of Tokyo researchers combine flexible printed structures with motor-driven wires to demonstrate supported stepping, offering a different take on bio-inspired robotics from Clone.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Apple's HALO Teaches a Unitree G1 to Navigate Unseen Rooms With Simulation-Generated Data
item.description: Trained on 300 hours of generated motion in simulated rooms, the onboard system completed 91% of 360 real-world trials without any teleoperation data.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: CMU Introduces Pixel, a Sub-$15,000 Wheeled Robot Designed to Learn From Human Demonstrations
item.description: Pixel combines a low-cost two-armed robot with human demonstration tools and whole-body learning. Its companion Pixel-UMI study reports 87% average task progress across five tasks.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)
